messages:
eli: Heads up — getting 404s from old crosslinks after the API reference migration. Looks like anchor slug rules differ between mkdocs and docusaurus for headings with inline code.

jo: Interesting. Example?

eli: On /docs/api/streaming the heading is: `### gRPC service `InferService``. MkDocs slugifies to `grpc-service-inferservice` but Docusaurus was emitting `grpc-service-inferservice` (different camel/underscore normalize) so older links like `/docs/api/streaming#grpc-service-inferservice` 404.

rahul: That mismatch rings a bell. Different slugify libs: mkdocs-plugin-slugify vs docusaurus-slugger. We saw similar when we moved the reference pages.

jo: Repro'd locally — linkcheck shows: `Broken fragment: /docs/api/streaming#grpc-service-inferservice -> 404`

build-bot: build failed — mkdocs-linkcheck 2 broken fragments detected (exit 1).

tara: Two paths forward: 1) canonicalize slugs in the build (preprocess headings to a single slug function) + add redirects for the old slugs, or 2) keep both slug variants by emitting duplicate id aliases (add extra id on the heading html). I prefer canonicalize + redirects. Cleaner long-term.

eli: Agreed. I can implement a small remark plugin that normalizes heading text with our chosen slug function (we'll use the mkdocs-style slug) during Docusaurus build so both sides match. Also add a _redirects mapping for the old slugs in the docs site.

jo: For discovery, here's a grep that finds headings with inline backticks: `git grep -n "^##.*`" -- docs | sed -e 's/:.*$//' | sort -u`

rahul: I ran a scan — ~7 pages contain inline code in headings (mainly API reference). I'll make a quick patch that: a) preprocess headings to strip/normalize inline code for slug generation, b) add `docs/_redirects` entries mapping the old mkdocs slug to the new one, c) add a remark-lint warning for inline code in headings.

build-bot: CI queued for PR 4678 (mkdocs/docusaurus slug harmonization + redirects).

jo: One gotcha — internal relative links in other docs currently point at the old slugs. We should run a repo-wide replace to update internal links to canonical slugs instead of only relying on redirects.

eli: Good call. I'll run a sed script to rewrite links after the slug rules are applied and include it in the PR as a one-off migration step.

tara: Also add a short note in the migration guide explaining how to reference service names in headings going forward (use plain text, avoid inline code).

build-bot: linkcheck initial run on branch: 7 broken fragments detected.

rahul: Pushed fixes + redirects file + migration note. Included a tiny test in docs-test that checks `slugify('gRPC service `InferService`') -> grpc-service-inferservice`.

jo: Re-running local linkcheck against the branch — now only 1 remaining broken fragment (some external doc had a hardcoded old slug).

build-bot: CI update: build passed, linkcheck passed :white_check_mark:. Redirects verified on staging.

eli: Merged PR 4678. I also pinged support & the migration channel with the redirect list so customers with bookmarked anchors won't hit 404s.

tara: Thanks — nice coordinated effort. If we still see anchor noise we can add a docs-health dashboard to surface fragment 404 spikes.

jo: +1 on the dashboard idea.

eli: Closing this thread. If anyone spots odd anchor fallout please reopen or DM. :wave:
